name: skeleton
summary: Loading placeholders swept by one angled light band across the whole screen.
props: Block width and height, in points or percent.
Corner radius. 'capsule' follows the kit radius for bars; 'full' is always a pill / circle.
Angled light band sweeping all blocks as one wave, a staggered top-to-bottom brighten, an opacity pulse, or no motion. Every variant is static when reduce motion is on.
Centred overlay inside the block (e.g. a faint glyph).
Paragraph placeholder with a slightly ragged edge.
{ aspectRatio, height, width, glyph, glyphSize, radius }
Image block with a faint picture glyph in the centre.
Rows with an avatar, two lines and a trailing pill.
Feed post: author row with menu, caption, media and an action bar.
{ header, back, actions, tabs, tabCount, rows, children }
Screen chrome while content loads — app bar, list body, bottom tabs.
Frame the shimmer / wave travels across, so blocks inside line up as one wave (Nav and Reveal add one).
{ loading, skeleton, children, stagger, animateHeight, loadingLabel }
Shows `skeleton` while loading; then it dissolves, top-level children rise in with a stagger and the height glides between the two.
Style for the block (composites apply it to their wrapper).
behavior: Every block reads one shared native-driver clock, so the shimmer band, wave or pulse moves across a Skeleton.Group (or the window) as a single sweep.
Every variant renders static, and Skeleton.Reveal swaps the skeleton for content instantly.
Placeholder blocks are hidden from screen readers. Skeleton.Reveal is marked busy and exposes a progressbar named by loadingLabel; the content arrives in a polite live region.
Plain Animated views plus a react-native-svg gradient, so it runs the same on iOS, Android and web.
usage:
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton';

<Skeleton.Group style={{ flexDirection: 'row', alignItems: 'center', gap: 12 }}>
  <Skeleton.Avatar size={44} />
  <Skeleton.Text lines={2} style={{ flex: 1 }} />
</Skeleton.Group>
